# Squish

> Squish is a free, privacy-focused image compression tool for writers and developers. It compresses PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF images (and HEIC in Safari) instantly in the browser with a live before/after comparison slider — no account, no uploads, and no server. All processing happens locally on the user's device, so images never leave the browser.

Squish is an open-source web application built with Nuxt 4 and published by the Illinois Criminal Justice Information Authority (ICJIA). Images are processed client-side with the HTML5 Canvas API; the original files are never modified and are never transmitted anywhere. The site's Content Security Policy names no third-party host. Re-encoding removes EXIF metadata, including GPS position. PNG output is lossless, so the quality setting affects only JPEG and WebP.

## How it works

- Drop, select or paste PNG, JPEG, WebP or AVIF images up to 50 MB (HEIC in Safari), or load the bundled sample image to try it.
- Optionally save as JPEG or WebP, and scale large images down to a chosen longest side.
- Adjust the quality slider (10–100%); color-coded guidance flags when quality may suffer.
- Drag the comparison slider to inspect original vs. compressed side by side; scroll to zoom (100–800%) and drag to pan.
- Download images individually or together as one ZIP file, with file sizes and savings shown inline.
- After the first visit the tool works offline.

## Features

- Client-side compression for PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF — images never leave the device
- Format conversion to JPEG or WebP, and resizing
- Works offline and can be installed as an app
- Live before/after comparison slider with zoom and pan
- Adjustable quality with real-time size and savings stats
- Batch processing with individual or ZIP download; paste from the clipboard
- Dark, responsive, WCAG 2.1 AA-accessible interface
